title: ReadWriteUntypedPositions
description: The positions --strict-read-write reaches a sub-schema through without the value ever being decoded into the type built for it. A prefixItems slot and a contains element are held in a []any, a patternProperties value in a map of raw JSON, and a schema whose whole shape is one of the unevaluated keywords is held as raw JSON with no fields at all -- so the two key lists a struct's decoder and encoder carry had nowhere to be, and the flag did nothing here (issue #219). Worse than nothing at three of them: the type built for the sub-schema was decoded into by a Validate check, so its readOnly refusal came back out of Validate() as a verdict about an annotation that constrains no document, which is exactly what #170 drew the line against. Each property below carries the same sub-schema -- one readOnly member, one writeOnly member, one that says nothing -- so a position that regresses names itself. `typedItems` is the control that already worked: a uniform items sub-schema becomes the element type and answers for itself. The sub-schema seals itself with additionalProperties:false so that its Validate depends on state the decoder fills in after the readOnly scan: a refusal returned from the middle of that decode leaves the overflow map empty, and the check a Validate path is there to make would then pass on a document it forbids. `child` is the same argument one level further down: the refusal arrives from a nested type through encoding/json, which records an Unmarshaler's error and goes on filling the rest of the value, so holding it is what keeps the value whole. `mapped` is what says a rule written for the members additionalProperties governs stops at the ones it does not: `decl` and any key matching ^p are claimed by name and by pattern, and each declares a plain `ro` that no keyword marks, so a walker stepping past neither would refuse a document the schema never marked. `viaThen` and `viaAnyOf` are the other boundary and are deliberately unbound: a subschema that was not selected contributes no annotation (2020-12 section 7.7.1), so a check keyed on one would refuse a document the schema never marked.
